title: Bearings & navigation
sentences: A bearing is measured clockwise from north: east is 090°, south is 180°, and west is 270°.
For east displacement E and north displacement N, a right triangle gives the straight-line distance.
The simple inverse-tangent ratio needs a quadrant check; atan2(E, N) handles all quadrants when normalized to 0°–360°.
Walk 3 km east, then 4 km north.
Find your displacement from the starting point.
E = 3 km and N = 4 km; the destination is northeast.
d = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, while the walked path was 7 km.
tan⁻¹(3/4) ≈ 36.87°, written as bearing 037° to the nearest degree.
